answer_text:
Here is a detailed **7-Day China Trip Itinerary** following the classic "Golden Triangle" route — **Beijing → Xi'an → Shanghai** — which is widely considered the best option for first-time visitors. This well-balanced itinerary covers popular destinations such as Beijing, Xi'an, and Shanghai, offering iconic attractions and convenient transportation.

---

## 🇨🇳 7-Day China Itinerary: Beijing → Xi'an → Shanghai

---

### 📅 Day 1 – Arrive in Beijing
Begin your journey in Beijing, where ancient history meets everyday local life. After landing, check into your hotel and take the rest of the day to recover from jet lag. Stroll around **Tiananmen Square** in the evening and soak in the atmosphere of the city.

> **Tip:** Take the Airport Express train to the city center for ¥25 — it's a better option than taxis during rush hour.

---

### 📅 Day 2 – Beijing: Forbidden City & Temple of Heaven
Visit the most iconic sights in and around the capital city, including the 15th-century Temple of Heaven, the Forbidden City, and the historic Tiananmen Square. In the evening, explore the nearby **hutong alleyways** for authentic local food and culture.

---

### 📅 Day 3 – Beijing: The Great Wall & Summer Palace
Dedicate today to the Great Wall. Visit the **Mutianyu section** of the Great Wall — it's less busy than Badaling and the views are better. Take the early bus to get more time at the wall. In the afternoon, head to the **Summer Palace**. The Summer Palace is an exceptional place that cannot be skipped from the Beijing itinerary. It's located 15 kilometers away from central Beijing and was used as a summer retreat by the Chinese royal family.

> **Tip:** At night, take the overnight train to Xi'an. Book a top bunk if you want more privacy at a lower price.

---

### 📅 Day 4 – Xi'an: Terracotta Army & Giant Wild Goose Pagoda
Marvel at the world-renowned **Terracotta Army**, an extraordinary underground army guarding China's first emperor. Later, visit the historic **Giant Wild Goose Pagoda**. An optional evening trip to **Great Tang All Day Mall** offers lively performances and Tang-style architecture.

> **Tip:** In the evening, check out the food stalls in the **Muslim Quarter**. Try Yang Rou Pao Mo, but ask them to go light on the oil if you're not used to rich food.

---

### 📅 Day 5 – Xi'an: City Wall & Travel to Shanghai
Ride a bike along the ancient **Xi'an City Wall**, one of the best-preserved city walls in China. You can rent a bike for ¥45 to ride the 14km wall circuit. Afterward, travel to Shanghai and experience China's dynamic modern face.

---

### 📅 Day 6 – Shanghai: The Bund, Yu Garden & Skyline
Begin with a visit to the **Shanghai Tower**, China's tallest building, offering panoramic views of the city. Then, unwind in the tranquil **Yu Garden**, a classical Chinese garden in the heart of the bustling metropolis. Wander through Yuyuan Bazaar and sample Shanghai's famous xiaolongbao (soup dumplings). In the afternoon, take a leisurely stroll along **Nanjing Road** before heading to **The Bund**, where colonial-era buildings blend seamlessly with futuristic skyscrapers.

---

### 📅 Day 7 – Shanghai: French Concession & Departure
Wander through the historic **Former French Concession**, known for its leafy streets and charming architecture. Visit the **Shanghai Museum** to gain deeper insight into Chinese art and history before heading to the airport for departure.

---

## 🗺️ Practical Travel Tips

- **Getting Between Cities:** These major cities have frequent high-speed trains and flights, giving you more flexibility and saving valuable travel time.
- **Visas:** China currently offers visa-free entry for up to 30 days to ordinary passport holders from 47 countries, including much of Europe, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Japan, and several South American nations — and a 7-day trip fits easily within this allowance.
- **Best Time to Visit:** China is a year-round destination for most of its popular regions. The main exceptions are high-altitude areas like Tibet and mountainous scenic spots such as Zhangjiajie and Huangshan, where heavy snow may close trails and limit access between December and February.
- **Apps & Language:** You may encounter internet limitations, language barriers, and a lack of English signage, but the availability of translation apps and tools will help overcome these challenges.

---

Enjoy your incredible adventure through China! 🏯🐉🌏
